aiOverview.content: iXAfrica Data Centres is the official colocation and host partner for Kenya's first Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) public cloud region in Nairobi.Announcement: Originally announced by President William Ruto in January 2024, the formal partnership with iXAfrica Data Centres was confirmed in January 2026.Host Location: Hosted at iXAfrica's NBOX1 campus located on Mombasa Road in Nairobi, Kenya (with a second campus, NBOX2, planned in the Tilisi development area).Infrastructure & Capacity:East and Central Africa's largest hyperscale, carrier-neutral, AI-ready data center.22 MW total campus capacity (featuring a 4.5 MW initial building and an 18 MW second phase).High-density AI capability supporting workloads up to 50 kW per rack using free-air cooling.Powered by Kenya's electrical grid, which relies on over 90% renewable energy (including geothermal power).Status: Listed as "Coming Soon" on Oracle's Public Cloud Regions directory, as full-scale operational rollout follows advanced deployment of construction and connectivity infrastructure.Strategic Impact: Provides Kenyan enterprises and public sector organizations with low-latency, sovereign, and data-residency-compliant cloud services without routing traffic through distant international regions.Would you like to know more about OCI cloud services or timelines/availability for enterprise onboarding in Nairobi?Would you like to know more about OCI cloud services or timelines/availability for enterprise onboarding in Nairobi? aiOverview.content: The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) proposed a standalone licensing framework in September 2026 to regulate data centers independently rather than grouping co-location facilities under the old Network Facilities Provider-Tier 2 (NFP-T2) regime.Standalone Licence Category: Replaces the previous NFP-T2 co-location classification to offer dedicated oversight for cloud, AI, and digital infrastructure expansion.Application Fee: Reported at Sh5,000 under the proposed structure.Licence Validity Period: Set for a 15-year term.Regulatory Intent: Improves operational visibility, streamlines market clarity, and aligns Kenya's digital infrastructure policies with comparable global jurisdictions.Consultation Timeline: Public participation and stakeholder feedback windows ran through late 2026 following initial policy notices.If you'd like, I can:Share details on how to file regulatory submissions or compliance notesSummarize differences between the old NFP-T2 rules and the new Data Centre categoryIf you'd like, I can:Share details on how to file regulatory submissions or compliance notesSummarize differences between the old NFP-T2 rules and the new Data Centre categoryAI responses may include mistakes.
